newsitem.title: GERMANY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN STILL FASTEST OF ALL.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN STILL FASTEST OF ALL.

text.p: Michael Doohan outclassed the opposition once again on Friday in opening qualifying for Sunday's German 500cc Grand Prix on a track he once hated.
The Australian, who has always been unlucky on the twisty and often rain-soaked Nuerburgring, clocked a fastest time of one minute 38.450 seconds on a miserable but dry day.
The three times world champion, winner of seven of the eight races held so far this season for Honda, left his rivals helpless in the first qualifying session.
Italian Luca Cadalora, on a Yamaha, clocked the second best time of 1:39.856 but he was a huge 1.406 of a second slower than the Australian.
Modenas rider Jean-Michel Bayle of France had the third fastest time of 1:39.881, an impressive showing for the new Kenny Roberts-built machine.
The track was six metres shorter than last year, with a change to the final chicane, but on Friday's form Doohan would certainly have broken the old circuit record.
"The new track is definitely an improvement," said Doohan. "It's more like it used to be when I first raced here some years ago."

The veteran from Brisbane came second to Cadalora last year after failing to make a last-ditch bid to regain the lead on the final lap because he had miscounted the laps and thought there was another to go.
The year before, he tumbled while leading and in the previous race staged here in 1990 he crashed heavily.
"I'm surprised to be so far ahead because this is not one of my favourite tracks," he said. "I tried to have a good day just in case it rains tomorrow."
All eyes were on local hope Ralf Waldmann in the 250cc session but the German, who won here last year, was only third best on his Honda.
Aprilia rider Loris Capirossi clocked the fastest time ahead of fellow Italian and world champion Max Biaggi, on a Honda.

In the 125cc class, Japanese Noboru Ueda was the fastest on a Honda while world championship leader Valentino Rossi of Italy, who has won six races already this season for Aprilia, had to be content with the fifth best time.

"Last year, I was pushing hard when (Japanese Masaki) Tokudome overtook me and crashed," said Rossi. "Maybe because of that, I was a little too cautious but anyway, I don't think it would have been possible to go as fast as Ueda."
